governanceNotes: D1 batch 37 (2026-09-23): deferred. Negative screen recorded 2026-09-23: (i) direction is inverted for outcome purposes - every located record documents underlying lesions producing Gerstmann manifestations rather than Gerstmann producing downstream outcomes: the Sanjo 2016 report documents progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy with left parietal white-matter lesions presenting with subacute dementia and Gerstmann syndrome, the Tanei 2012 report documents metastatic melanoma lesions in the frontal and parietal lobes presenting with Gerstmann symptoms alongside hemiparesis and consciousness disturbance, and the Russell 2005 series of 28 consecutive parietal-lobe glioma resections documents the components of Gerstmann syndrome as the association deficits of large dominant-hemisphere tumors involving both superior and inferior parietal lobules with deficits appearing and resolving with resection; (ii) zero-record outcome screening - Gerstmann-specific downstream outcome queries return lesion-cause reports and pediatric neurodevelopmental descriptions only, with no Gerstmann-specific depression, anxiety, or functional-outcome quantification isolated from the underlying-lesion cohorts because the syndrome is scored as a sign of parietal pathology rather than a followed exposure; (iii) constitutive-component barrier - agraphia, acalculia, finger agnosia, and left-right disorientation are the syndrome itself, so mapping them to a separate cognitive-disorder identity would assert a phenotype onto itself (the ME-41 phenotype barrier the batch-33 peritoneal-adhesions rejection enforced), while the genuinely upstream identities (cerebrovascular-accident-stroke-residuals, brain-tumors, brain-cancer) already exist and own the lesion-to-deficit direction; (iv) no catalog identity fits the functional outcomes the syndrome could plausibly contribute to (academic/occupational disability has no identity), so no non-duplicative, direction-correct edge exists today. Reopening condition: a directional cohort of Gerstmann patients with a catalog-fit outcome and documented chronology, or Gerstmann-specific outcome quantification.
